26: pub(super) fn measure(
27:     input: &TacticalSceneInput,
28:     source: &GeographicSurface,
29:     terrain: &SceneTerrain,
30: ) -> Result<Value, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
31:     let composed = terrain
32:         .physical_geographic_surface()
33:         .ok_or("production terrain has no admitted support surface")?;
34:     let gardens: Vec<_> = input.gardens.iter().map(|garden| {
35:         let regions: Vec<_> = outlines(garden)?.into_iter().map(|region|
36:             measure_region(&region, source, &composed)).collect::<Result<Vec<_>,_>>()?;
37:         let roots = adventuresim_tactical_core::scene_input::SceneGarden::project(garden.clone(), terrain);
38:         Ok(json!({"property_id":garden.owner,"member_building_ids":[garden.front_building_id],"regions":regions,
39:             "geometry_validation":garden.validate_geometry(&input.streets),
40:             "root_projection": match roots { Ok(roots) => json!({"pass":true,"plant_support":roots.plant_support()}),
41:                 Err(error) => json!({"pass":false,"error":error.to_string()}) }}))
42:     }).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>>>()?;
43:     Ok(
44:         json!({"scope":"Complete soil envelope, bed, route and plant-hull triangle intersections, before and after grading. A soil envelope can include its front building's occupied footprint; working beds, lanes and planting hulls must be clear. Construction grade is recorded separately from the authored controller's walking limit. Complete unchanged-source route comparisons bound introduced ledges; controller traversal and collision clearance are separate acceptance checks.","observations":gardens}),
45:     )

48: fn outlines(garden: &CityGarden) -> Result<Vec<GardenRegionOutline>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
49:     let routes = garden.access.iter().enumerate().map(|(index, route)| {
50:         let tangent = route.end_metres() - route.start_metres();
51:         let bounds = CityPlotBounds::new(adventuresim_tactical_core::scene_coordinates::ScenePlanPoint::try_from((route.start_metres() + route.end_metres()) * 0.5)?,adventuresim_building_generator::spatial_geometry::PlanDimensions::from_metres(Vec2::new(
52:                 tangent.length() + route.half_width_metres() * 2.0,
53:                 route.half_width_metres() * 2.0,
54:             ))?,BuildingOrientation::from_frontage_tangent(tangent)
55:                 .ok_or(adventuresim_building_generator::spatial_geometry::GeometryError::InvalidProjection)?)?;
56:         Ok(GardenRegionOutline { kind: GardenRegion::Route, index: Some(index), outline: bounds.corners().to_vec() })
57:     }).collect::<Result<Vec<_>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>>>()?;
58:     Ok(std::iter::once(GardenRegionOutline {
59:         kind: GardenRegion::SoilEnvelope,
60:         index: None,
61:         outline: garden.cultivated_bounds.corners().to_vec(),
62:     })
63:     .chain(
64:         garden
65:             .beds
66:             .iter()
67:             .enumerate()
68:             .map(|(i, bed)| GardenRegionOutline {
69:                 kind: GardenRegion::Bed,
70:                 index: Some(i),
71:                 outline: bed.corners().to_vec(),
72:             }),
73:     )
74:     .chain(routes)
75:     .chain(
76:         garden
77:             .plants
78:             .iter()
79:             .enumerate()
80:             .map(|(i, plant)| GardenRegionOutline {
81:                 kind: GardenRegion::PlantHull,
82:                 index: Some(i),
83:                 outline: plant.world_hull(),
84:             }),
85:     )
86:     .collect())
87: }

89: fn measure_region(
90:     region: &GardenRegionOutline,
91:     source: &GeographicSurface,
92:     composed: &GeographicSurface,
93: ) -> Result<Value, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
94:     let GardenRegionOutline {
95:         kind,
96:         index,
97:         outline,
98:     } = region;
99:     let contact = f64::from(
100:         CompoundGradingPolicy::bounded_settlement()
101:             .limits
102:             .contact_tolerance_metres(),
103:     );
104:     let perimeter: f64 = outline
105:         .iter()
106:         .zip(outline.iter().cycle().skip(1))
107:         .take(outline.len())
108:         .map(|(a, b)| a.as_dvec2().distance(b.as_dvec2()))
109:         .sum();
110:     let area_bound = perimeter * CityPlotBounds::COORDINATE_TOLERANCE_METRES;
111:     let admitted =
112:         adventuresim_tactical_core::scene_coordinates::ScenePlanPolygon::from_ordered_vertices(
113:             outline
114:                 .iter()
115:                 .copied()
116:                 .map(adventuresim_tactical_core::scene_coordinates::ScenePlanPoint::try_from)
117:                 .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()?,
118:         )?;
119:     let measurement = source.measure_region(&admitted);
120:     let composed_measurement = composed.measure_region(&admitted);
121:     let comparison = source.compare_in_outline(composed, &admitted);
122:     let motor = TacticalCombatConfig::default().movement.motor;
123:     let walk_grade = f64::from(motor.maximum_walkable_slope_degrees)
124:         .to_radians()
125:         .tan();

204: fn nearest_fault_scarp(
205:     terrain_features: &[TerrainFeature],
206:     center: Wgs84CoordinateE7,
207:     seed: fabelgeist_determinism::Seed,
208: ) -> Option<TerrainLandformRecipe> {
209:     let latitude = center.latitude().degrees();
210:     let longitude = center.longitude().degrees();
211:     let longitude_scale =
212:         (METRES_PER_LATITUDE_DEGREE * latitude.to_radians().cos()).max(MIN_LONGITUDE_SCALE);
213:     let playable_half_extent =
214:         f64::from(PLAYABLE_SIDE - 1) * f64::from(PLAYABLE_SPACING_METRES) * 0.5;
215:     let mut nearest: Option<(f64, [f64; 2], [i32; 2], TerrainLandformLod)> = None;
216:     for feature in terrain_features {
217:         let TerrainFeature::MappedFault(fault) = feature else {
218:             continue;
219:         };
220:         for segment in fault.trace.windows(2) {
221:             let a = [
222:                 (segment[0].longitude() - longitude) * longitude_scale,
223:                 (segment[0].latitude() - latitude) * METRES_PER_LATITUDE_DEGREE,
224:             ];
225:             let b = [
226:                 (segment[1].longitude() - longitude) * longitude_scale,
227:                 (segment[1].latitude() - latitude) * METRES_PER_LATITUDE_DEGREE,
228:             ];
229:             let tangent = [b[0] - a[0], b[1] - a[1]];
230:             let length_squared = tangent[0] * tangent[0] + tangent[1] * tangent[1];
231:             if length_squared < 1.0 {
232:                 continue;
233:             }
234:             let fraction =
235:                 (-(a[0] * tangent[0] + a[1] * tangent[1]) / length_squared).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
236:             let closest = [a[0] + tangent[0] * fraction, a[1] + tangent[1] * fraction];
237:             let origin_cm = [
238:                 (closest[0] * 100.0).round() as i32,
239:                 (closest[1] * 100.0).round() as i32,
240:             ];

338: /// Contact energy describes the local collision, not whole-body kinetic
339: /// energy. This transfer scale makes the canonical default's ordinary ~49.5 J punch
340: /// move an 80 kg equipped bandit about 0.25 m under the tactical controller's
341: /// standard grounded friction.
342: /// Converts combat contact energy into an explicit physical delta-v. Combat
343: /// resolution historically calls the energy-like value `contact_force`; this
344: /// seam prevents those joules from being mistaken for either newtons or an
345: /// already mass-normalized impulse.
346: fn hit_velocity_change(
347:     result: AttackResult,
348:     attacker_position: Vec3,
349:     defender_position: Vec3,
350:     attacker_mass_kg: f32,
351:     defender_mass_kg: f32,
352:     config: &ImpactConfig,
353: ) -> (bool, Vec3) {
354:     let (hits_attacker, contact_energy, mass) = match result {
355:         AttackResult::ToAttacker { contact_force, .. } => {
356:             (true, contact_force.max(0.0), attacker_mass_kg)
357:         }
358:         AttackResult::ToDefender { contact_force, .. } => {
359:             (false, contact_force.max(0.0), defender_mass_kg)
360:         }

361:     };
362:     if !contact_energy.is_finite() || contact_energy <= 0.0 {
363:         return (hits_attacker, Vec3::ZERO);
364:     }
365:     let horizontal = (defender_position - attacker_position)
366:         .xz()
367:         .normalize_or_zero();
368:     if horizontal == Vec2::ZERO {
369:         return (hits_attacker, Vec3::ZERO);
370:     }
371:     let horizontal = if hits_attacker {
372:         -horizontal
373:     } else {
374:         horizontal
375:     };
376:     let direction = Vec3::new(horizontal.x, 0.0, horizontal.y);
377:     let speed = ((2.0 * contact_energy / mass.max(1.0)).sqrt() * config.whole_body_velocity_scale)
378:         .min(
379:             config
380:                 .maximum_velocity_change_metres_per_second
381:                 .metres_per_second(),
382:         );
383:     (hits_attacker, direction * speed)
384: }

422: fn ranged_target_in_aim_cone(
423:     yaw: f32,
424:     attacker: Vec3,
425:     target: Vec3,
426:     half_angle_degrees: f32,
427: ) -> bool {
428:     let offset = target.xz() - attacker.xz();

431:     };

433:     direction.dot(forward) >= half_angle_degrees.to_radians().cos()
434: }

1689: /// Records the controller result after Ahoy has applied collision constraints.
1690: /// `apply_character_motor` emits the matching pre-collision sample with the
1691: /// same skeleton and push ticks.
1692: pub(crate) fn trace_authoritative_quickstep_after_collision(players: QuickstepTraceQuery<'_, '_>) {
1693:     for (entity, skeleton, push, transform, velocity, controller) in &players {
1694:         if !push.active {
1695:             continue;
1696:         }
1697:         let world_direction = (push.orientation
1698:             * Vec3::new(push.direction.x, 0.0, -push.direction.y))
1699:         .xz()
1700:         .normalize_or_zero();
1701:         let displacement_vector = (transform.translation - push.origin).xz();
1702:         info!(
1703:             target: "quickstep_trace",
1704:             ?entity,
1705:             skeleton_tick = skeleton.locomotion_sample_tick.encoded(),
1706:             push_start_tick = push.start_tick.encoded(),
1707:             elapsed_ticks = skeleton
1708:                 .locomotion_sample_tick
1709:                 .saturating_sub(push.start_tick).samples(),
1710:             ?world_direction,
1711:             translation = ?transform.translation,
1712:             ?displacement_vector,
1713:             forward_displacement = displacement_vector.dot(world_direction),
1714:             linear_velocity = ?velocity.0,
1715:             forward_velocity = velocity.xz().dot(world_direction),
1716:             grounded = ?controller.grounded,
1717:             "[quickstep][server-post-collision] resolved controller"
1718:         );
1719:     }
1720: }

101: #[derive(Debug, Error)]
102: pub enum IconError {
103:     #[error("icon dimensions or supersampling are invalid")]
104:     InvalidSpec,
105:     #[error("weapon generation failed: {0}")]
106:     Generate(#[from] GenerateError),
107:     #[error("weapon has no usable icon focus geometry")]
108:     MissingFocus,
109:     #[error("weapon icon rasterization failed")]
110:     Rasterization,
111:     #[error("weapon icon PNG encoding failed: {0}")]
112:     Png(String),
113: }
114: 
115: /// Presentation classification is derived from component semantics, not catalog IDs.
116: /// This keeps arbitrary modular polearm heads in the head-focused family.
117: pub fn icon_layout(design: &WeaponDesign) -> WeaponIconLayout {
118:     let has_guard = design
119:         .recipe
120:         .components
121:         .iter()
122:         .any(|component| component.role == Some(ComponentRole::Guard));
123:     let has_sword_blade = design
124:         .recipe
125:         .components
126:         .iter()
127:         .any(|component| matches!(component.shape, crate::recipe::Shape::LoftedBlade(_)));
128:     if has_guard && has_sword_blade {
129:         WeaponIconLayout::HiltFocus
130:     } else {
131:         WeaponIconLayout::HeadFocus
132:     }
133: }
134: 
135: pub fn generate_icon(design: &WeaponDesign, spec: WeaponIconSpec) -> Result<WeaponIcon, IconError> {
136:     let generated = generate(design)?;
137:     let layout = icon_layout(design);
138:     let projection = Projection::new(design, &generated, layout)?;
139:     rasterize_icon(&generated.parts, spec, projection)
140: }
141: 
142: /// Render a fitted scabbard or haft loop from its independently persisted recipe.
143: ///
144: /// Blade sheaths use the same diagonal as their weapon, with the throat centered
145: /// and the long body intentionally cropped toward the lower-left. Compact haft
146: /// loops fit the complete loop-and-hanger assembly in the opposite diagonal.
147: pub fn generate_holder_icon(
148:     design: &WeaponHolderDesign,
149:     spec: WeaponIconSpec,
150: ) -> Result<WeaponIcon, IconError> {
151:     let generated = generate_holder(design)?;
152:     let projection = Projection::holder(&generated)?;
153:     rasterize_icon(&generated.parts, spec, projection)
154: }
155: 
156: fn rasterize_icon(
157:     parts: &[MeshPart],
158:     spec: WeaponIconSpec,
159:     projection: Projection,
160: ) -> Result<WeaponIcon, IconError> {
161:     let (rgba, alpha) = render::render(parts, spec, &projection)?;
162:     let output_size = usize::from(spec.size);
163:     let occupied_bounds = occupied_bounds(&alpha, output_size).ok_or(IconError::Rasterization)?;
164:     Ok(WeaponIcon {
165:         size: spec.size,
166:         rgba,
167:         layout: projection.layout,
168:         mirrored: projection.mirror_x,
169:         framing_anchor: projection.framing_anchor,
170:         head_zoom: projection.head_zoom,
171:         focus_bounds: projection.focus_bounds,

173:     })
174: }

3905: pub fn valid_settlement_name(value: &str) -> bool {
3906:     !value.trim().is_empty()
3907:         && value.chars().count() <= MAX_SETTLEMENT_NAME_CHARS
3908:         && !value.chars().any(char::is_control)
3909: }

3911: fn deserialize_settlement_name<'de, D>(deserializer: D) -> Result<String, D::Error>
3912: where
3913:     D: serde::Deserializer<'de>,
3914: {
3915:     let value = String::deserialize(deserializer)?;
3916:     if valid_settlement_name(&value) {
3917:         Ok(value)
3918:     } else {
3919:         Err(serde::de::Error::custom(
3920:             "settlement name must contain 1 to 160 non-control characters",
3921:         ))
3922:     }
3923: }

1: //! Shells of any topology, evaluated vertex by vertex on the device.
   2: //!
   3: //! Where a plate is not a grid of rows and columns -- a dome's pole and
   4: //! rings, a skirt hung from part of a rim, a torso's panels joined by seams,
   5: //! a visor pierced by a triangulated domain -- the host decides every
   6: //! vertex and triangle from the design. It gives each vertex four floats of
   7: //! coordinates whose meaning the shape defines, and the shape's WGSL turns
   8: //! them into a point:
   9: //!
  10: //! ```wgsl
  11: //! fn shell_vertex(index: u32, coord: vec4<f32>) -> ShellVertex
  12: //! ```
  13: //!
  14: //! `index` is the vertex's index within the shell. A vertex that depends on
  15: //! others -- a seam point between two panels, a cap ring gathered from a
  16: //! rim -- belongs to a later pass: `shell_pass(index, coord)` names it, and
  17: //! the kernel runs once per pass, so a later pass can read what an earlier one
  18: //! wrote through `local_carrier(index)`.

  21: 
  22: use fabelgeist_compute::{Kernel, KernelBatch};

  26: use super::{ArmorGpu, device_error, wgsl};
  27: use crate::{BoundaryNormals, GenerateError};
  28: 
  29: /// One shell whose vertices the host lists with their coordinates.
  30: #[derive(Clone, Debug)]
  31: pub struct CoordShell {
  32:     pub coords: Vec<[f32; 4]>,
  33:     pub indices: Vec<u32>,
  34:     pub boundary_normals: BoundaryNormals,
  35:     pub thickness: f32,
  36:     pub extrusion: CoordExtrusion,
  37:     /// Shape constants that differ between the shells of one part.
  38:     pub values: [f32; 4],
  39:     /// Reflected across its local x before the part frame places it.
  40:     pub mirrored: bool,
  41:     /// Which of the part's frames places this shell.
  42:     pub frame: usize,
  43:     /// Passes the shell's vertices are evaluated in.
  44:     pub passes: u32,
  45:     /// Where this shell's `shell_hinge()` is written, if it carries one.

  49: /// How a coordinate shell is thickened; origins and axes are local and may

  51: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]

  58: impl CoordExtrusion {
  59:     fn parts(self) -> (Extrusion, [f32; 3], [f32; 3]) {

101:     /// read before triangulation; final device failures are reported by

 103:     pub async fn record(
 104:         gpu: &ArmorGpu,
 105:         mut batch: KernelBatch<'_>,

 107:         torso: TorsoBody<'_>,

   9: use fabelgeist_shell::ParticleArealDensity;

  13: pub struct Fabric {
  14:     /// Areal density, kg per square metre. Sets the particle masses, and with
  15:     /// them how the cloth hangs.
  16:     pub density: ParticleArealDensity,
  17:     /// Resistance to stretching along the mesh edges. Near zero for anything
  18:     /// woven: real cloth barely stretches in the warp and weft.
  19:     pub stretch_compliance: f32,
  20:     /// Resistance to bending at the hinge between two triangles. This is the
  21:     /// parameter that decides whether the fabric falls in a few heavy folds or
  22:     /// many light ones, and it is the one worth exposing to a user.
  23:     ///
  24:     /// The useful range is roughly `1e-6` (a board) to `1e-3` (a rag); the

  27:     /// mesh's length scale -- see `topology::bending_weights`.
  28:     pub bend_compliance: f32,
  29:     /// Resistance at a seam. Stiffer than the fabric itself, because a sewn
  30:     /// seam is two layers plus thread.
  31:     pub seam_compliance: f32,

  34:     pub thickness: f32,

  36:     pub friction: f32,
  37:     /// Velocity drag, per second. Air resistance, in effect: it is what stops

  39:     pub damping: f32,

1: //! The cached dispatch path.
   2: //!
   3: //! [`ComputePass::record`] builds a uniform buffer and a bind group for every
   4: //! dispatch. That is fine at a handful of dispatches per frame, which is what
   5: //! the other primitives here do. A solver is different: an XPBD step is
   6: //! substeps times constraint colours, comfortably five hundred dispatches in a
   7: //! frame, and allocating two GPU objects for each of them costs more in CPU
   8: //! time than the shaders cost on the GPU -- and, run at speed, exhausts the
   9: //! allocator outright.
  10: //!
  11: //! So a [`Kernel`](super::Kernel) builds its own pipeline with a
  12: //! **dynamic-offset** uniform and a ring of uniform slots, written by offset,
  13: //! so the per-dispatch values cost a `write_buffer` into memory that already
  14: //! exists rather than a fresh allocation.
  15: //!
  16: //! # The bind group is *not* cached, deliberately
  17: //!
  18: //! Caching it is the obvious next step and it is wrong. Reusing one bind group
  19: //! across consecutive compute passes makes wgpu's resource tracker treat the
  20: //! buffers as already in the right state, and it stops emitting the barrier
  21: //! between them -- so a dispatch can start reading what the previous one has
  22: //! not finished writing. It shows up as a solver that is subtly, intermittently
  23: //! wrong: in the case that found this, a refit BVH that had lost a few
  24: //! primitives, failing about two runs in three.
  25: //!
  26: //! Creating the bind group per dispatch re-registers the resources and the
  27: //! barrier comes back. Measured on a full garment step, that costs six per
  28: //! cent -- 4.7 ms a frame against 4.4 -- which is not a trade worth making.
  29: //! The expensive part was never the bind group; it was allocating a uniform
  30: //! *buffer* per dispatch, and the ring is what fixes that.
  31: //!
  32: //! Kernels whose shape this cannot serve -- more than one bind group, or any
  33: //! texture or sampler binding -- have no fast path and fall back to
  34: //! `ComputePass::record`, which still handles everything.
  35: 
  36: use crate::prelude::*;
  37: use fabelgeist_gpu::data::gpu::buffer::Buffer;
  38: use fabelgeist_gpu::data::gpu::parameters::{PassParameter, PassParameters};
  39: use fabelgeist_gpu::data::gpu::shader::{BufferBinding, UniformMember};
  40: 
  41: /// Bytes in each buffer of a batch's [`UniformArena`].
  42: const CHUNK_BYTES: u64 = 64 * 1024;
  43: 
  44: /// The largest uniform block the cached path packs without allocating.
  45: ///
  46: /// Every kernel here passes a few scalars and at most a vector or two. A
  47: /// kernel wanting more than this is refused a fast path rather than silently
  48: /// allocating per dispatch, which is the cost this whole module exists to
  49: /// avoid.
  50: const MAX_UNIFORM_BYTES: usize = 256;
  51: 
  52: pub(super) struct FastPath {
  53:     pipeline: wgpu::ComputePipeline,
  54:     layout: wgpu::BindGroupLayout,
  55: 
  56:     buffers: Vec<BufferBinding>,
  57:     uniform_binding: Option<u32>,
  58:     uniform_members: Vec<UniformMember>,
  59:     uniform_size: u64,
  60:     /// `uniform_size` rounded up to the device's binding alignment.
  61:     stride: u64,
  62: }
  63: 
  64: struct CompiledLayout {
  65:     layout: wgpu::BindGroupLayout,
  66:     pipeline: wgpu::ComputePipeline,
  67: }
  68: 
  69: /// The uniform values of one batch's dispatches.
  70: ///
  71: /// A kernel used to own a ring of uniform slots that every batch wrote into
  72: /// in turn. A ring is only safe to wrap once the batch holding a slot has been
  73: /// submitted, and with several threads recording at once nothing guarantees
  74: /// that: a long batch still being recorded on one thread saw its slots
  75: /// overwritten by other threads' dispatches, and ran with their counts. So
  76: /// each batch now writes its uniforms into buffers of its own, which live
  77: /// exactly as long as its commands need them.
  78: #[derive(Default)]
  79: pub(super) struct UniformArena {
  80:     chunks: Vec<wgpu::Buffer>,
  81:     /// Bytes used in the last chunk.
  82:     used: u64,
  83: }
  84: 
  85: impl UniformArena {
  86:     /// Room for one dispatch's uniform block: the buffer and its offset.
  87:     fn allocate(&mut self, context: &WgpuContext, stride: u64) -> (wgpu::Buffer, u64) {
  88:         if self.chunks.is_empty() || self.used + stride > CHUNK_BYTES {
  89:             // Created mapped, so that it is initialised from the start rather
  90:             // than zero-filled lazily around the submission that reads it.
  91:             let chunk = context.device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
  92:                 label: Some("Kernel Uniform Arena"),
  93:                 size: CHUNK_BYTES,
  94:                 usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::UNIFORM | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST,
  95:                 mapped_at_creation: true,
  96:             });
  97:             chunk.unmap();
  98:             self.chunks.push(chunk);
  99:             self.used = 0;
 100:         }
 101:         let offset = self.used;
 102:         self.used += stride;
 103:         (self.chunks.last().expect("allocated above").clone(), offset)
 104:     }
 105: }
 106: 
 107: /// What a prepared dispatch needs at record time.
 108: pub(super) struct Prepared {
 109:     pub pipeline: wgpu::ComputePipeline,
 110:     pub bind_group: wgpu::BindGroup,
 111:     pub dynamic_offset: Option<u32>,
 112: }
 113: 
 114: impl CompiledLayout {
 115:     fn new(
 116:         context: &WgpuContext,
 117:         entries: &[wgpu::BindGroupLayoutEntry],
 118:         module: &wgpu::ShaderModule,
 119:         entry_point: &str,
 120:     ) -> Result<Self> {
 121:         #[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
 122:         let error_scope = context.blocking_validation.then(|| {
 123:             context
 124:                 .device
 125:                 .push_error_scope(wgpu::ErrorFilter::Validation)
 126:         });
 127:         let layout = context
 128:             .device
 129:             .create_bind_group_layout(&wgpu::BindGroupLayoutDescriptor {
 130:                 label: Some("Kernel Bind Layout"),
 131:                 entries,
 132:             });
 133:         let pipeline_layout =
 134:             context
 135:                 .device
 136:                 .create_pipeline_layout(&wgpu::PipelineLayoutDescriptor {
 137:                     label: Some("Kernel Pipeline Layout"),
 138:                     bind_group_layouts: &[Some(&layout)],
 139:                     immediate_size: 0,
 140:                 });
 141:         let pipeline = context
 142:             .device
 143:             .create_compute_pipeline(&wgpu::ComputePipelineDescriptor {
 144:                 label: Some("Kernel Pipeline"),
 145:                 layout: Some(&pipeline_layout),
 146:                 module,
 147:                 entry_point: Some(entry_point),
 148:                 compilation_options: wgpu::PipelineCompilationOptions::default(),
 149:                 cache: None,
 150:             });

1: //! Measuring a body mesh into the measurements a pattern is drawn from.
   2: //!
   3: //! A GarmentCode pattern is made to measure: every panel's size comes from a
   4: //! [`Body`], the twenty-six numbers a tailor would take. The bundled bodies
   5: //! are averages, so drawing a pattern from one and then putting it on somebody
   6: //! else's body is a garment made for a different person -- which is what
   7: //! scaling a body model to the pattern's height amounts to. This module goes
   8: //! the other way: it takes the measurements off the mesh, so the pattern is
   9: //! drawn for the body it will be worn by.
  10: //!
  11: //! # What the mesh has to be
  12: //!
  13: //! * A closed triangle mesh of a standing body, in **centimetres**, the unit
  14: //!   GarmentCode measures in.
  15: //! * `+y` up, `+x` to the body's **left**, `+z` in **front** of it. The floor
  16: //!   is wherever the lowest vertex is; nothing has to be centred.
  17: //! * Standing, legs apart enough to be separate below the crotch, arms away
  18: //!   from the body far enough to be separate below the armpit. Any A-pose or
  19: //!   T-pose qualifies; arms straight down the sides do not, because the armpit
  20: //!   is found by looking for where the arms leave the torso.
  21: //!
  22: //! # What the caller has to supply
  23: //!
  24: //! Six pairs of joint positions, in [`Landmarks`]. Everything else is taken
  25: //! off the surface. The joints are needed because some measurements are about
  26: //! the skeleton rather than the skin -- the arm's length, the shoulder line a
  27: //! sleeve is aligned to, the angle the arm is held at -- and because they say
  28: //! where to look for the rest: which cut is a thigh and which is a calf.
  29: //!
  30: //! # How the levels are found
  31: //!
  32: //! Nothing is at a fixed fraction of the height. Each level is the answer to a
  33: //! question about the surface, so a short broad body and a tall narrow one are
  34: //! each measured at their own waist rather than at the average person's:
  35: //!
  36: //! * **crotch** -- the highest cut at which the legs are still two rings.
  37: //! * **hips** -- the widest cut between the crotch and the waist.
  38: //! * **waist** -- the narrowest cut between the hip joints and the ribs.
  39: //! * **armpit** -- the highest cut at which the arms are still their own rings.
  40: //! * **bust** -- the widest cut between the waist and the armpit.
  41: //! * **underbust** -- the narrowest cut between the waist and the bust.
  42: //! * **neck base** -- the lowest cut above the shoulders that is one ring and
  43: //!   narrower than half the shoulders.
  44: //!
  45: //! The one measurement that is not taken off the surface is `head_l`, the nape
  46: //! to the top of the head, which is Euclidean because GarmentCode's own
  47: //! documentation says so.
  48: 
  49: use anyhow::{Result, bail};
  50: 
  51: use crate::Body;
  52: 
  53: mod section;
  54: 
  55: pub use section::BodyMesh;
  56: use section::{Axes, Ring, back_width, cross_section, flatten, flatten_on_plane, hull, perimeter};
  57: 
  58: /// The joints a measurement needs from whichever rig posed the mesh.
  59: ///
  60: /// Each pair is `[left, right]`, in the same centimetre frame as the mesh.
  61: /// Which is which only matters for the sign of `x`; every measurement that
  62: /// uses a pair either averages them or takes one.
  63: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
  64: pub struct Landmarks {
  65:     /// The shoulder joints -- where the upper arm turns in its socket. The
  66:     /// line between them is `shoulder_w`, which is what a sleeve is aligned
  67:     /// to.
  68:     pub shoulders: [[f32; 3]; 2],
  69:     pub elbows: [[f32; 3]; 2],
  70:     pub wrists: [[f32; 3]; 2],
  71:     /// The hip joints -- where the thigh turns. Used to say where a thigh is,
  72:     /// and as the bottom of the range the waist is looked for in.
  73:     pub hips: [[f32; 3]; 2],
  74:     pub knees: [[f32; 3]; 2],
  75:     /// The base of the neck, roughly. Only used to say where to start looking
  76:     /// for the neck on the surface, so it does not have to be exact.
  77:     pub neck: [f32; 3],
  78: }
  79: 
  80: /// How finely the body is scanned when a level is looked for, as a fraction of
  81: /// the body's height.
  82: ///
  83: /// A body is scanned a few hundred times over, so this is the cost of a
  84: /// measurement; two thousandths of a height is about 3 mm on an adult, which
  85: /// is finer than the levels themselves are defined.
  86: const SCAN_STEP: f32 = 0.002;
  87: 
  88: /// Take the measurements off a body mesh.
  89: pub fn measure(mesh: BodyMesh<'_>, landmarks: &Landmarks) -> Result<Body> {
  90:     if mesh.vertices.is_empty() || mesh.faces.is_empty() {
  91:         bail!("the body mesh is empty");
  92:     }
  93: 
  94:     let measurer = Measurer::new(mesh, landmarks)?;
  95:     measurer.body()
  96: }
  97: 
  98: struct Measurer<'a> {
  99:     mesh: BodyMesh<'a>,
 100:     marks: Landmarks,
 101:     floor: f32,
 102:     top: f32,
 103:     /// The body's own middle, side to side and front to back, from the torso
 104:     /// rather than from the whole mesh: outstretched arms would drag the
 105:     /// average sideways and a foot forwards.
 106:     axis: [f32; 2],
 107:     step: f32,
 108: }
 109: 
 110: /// A level found on the body, with the section that was found there.
 111: struct Level {
 112:     y: f32,
 113:     girth: f32,
 114:     hull: Vec<[f32; 2]>,
 115:     ring: Ring,
 116: }
 117: 
 118: impl<'a> Measurer<'a> {
 119:     fn new(mesh: BodyMesh<'a>, landmarks: &Landmarks) -> Result<Self> {
 120:         let mut floor = f32::INFINITY;
 121:         let mut top = f32::NEG_INFINITY;
 122:         for vertex in mesh.vertices {
 123:             floor = floor.min(vertex[1]);
 124:             top = top.max(vertex[1]);
 125:         }
 126:         // GarmentCode measures in centimetres, and a mesh in metres is the
 127:         // mistake this will be made with: it would measure without complaint
 128:         // and produce a pattern for a doll.
 129:         let height = top - floor;
 130:         if !height.is_finite() || height <= 50.0 {
 131:             bail!(
 132:                 "the body mesh is {:.3} tall; measurements are in centimetres,                  so a standing body should be over 50",
 133:                 height
 134:             );
 135:         }
 136: 
 137:         // The hip joints are inside the pelvis, so their middle is the body's
 138:         // axis whatever the arms and feet are doing.
 139:         let hips = landmarks.hips;
 140:         let axis = [
 141:             (hips[0][0] + hips[1][0]) / 2.0,
 142:             (hips[0][2] + hips[1][2]) / 2.0,
 143:         ];
 144: 
 145:         Ok(Self {
 146:             mesh,
 147:             marks: *landmarks,
 148:             floor,
 149:             top,
 150:             axis,
 151:             step: (top - floor) * SCAN_STEP,
 152:         })
 153:     }
 154: 
 155:     fn height(&self) -> f32 {
 156:         self.top - self.floor
 157:     }
 158: 
 159:     /// The rings of a horizontal cut.
 160:     fn cut(&self, y: f32) -> Vec<Ring> {

1: //! Turning a sewing pattern into simulated cloth.
   2: //!
   3: //! `fabelgeist-garment-code` produces a [`PatternSpec`]: flat panels, each with a
   4: //! placement around the body, and a list of which edge is sewn to which.
   5: //! `fabelgeist-cloth` wants panels as plain outlines and seams as edge pairs. This
   6: //! is the adapter between them, plus the driver that steps the result against
   7: //! an MHR body.
   8: //!
   9: //! The two libraries know nothing about each other, and neither depends on the
  10: //! other -- which is the point. `fabelgeist-cloth` sits in the prism workspace and
  11: //! would be just as happy with a pattern from anywhere else.
  12: //!
  13: //! [`pose`] is the third piece: the pattern's placement is drawn for a set of
  14: //! measurements rather than for the body in front of it, so the garment can
  15: //! be moved onto that body before the solver is allowed to start.
  16: 
  17: use fabelgeist_cloth::garment::{Panel, Placement, Seam, SeamSide};
  18: use fabelgeist_cloth::{Cloth, Fabric, GarmentMesh};
  19: use fabelgeist_compute::prelude::KernelCache;
  20: use fabelgeist_garment_code::pattern::PatternSpec;
  21: use fabelgeist_gpu::prelude::WgpuContext;
  22: use fabelgeist_math::{Vec2, Vec3};
  23: use fabelgeist_physics::{Collider, Collisions, MeshCollider, MeshSurface};
  24: use fabelgeist_xpbd::{Solver, SolverSettings};
  25: 
  26: pub mod pose;
  27: 
  28: pub use pose::{GarmentPose, Pivots};
  29: 
  30: /// A sewing pattern is measured in centimetres; the solver works in metres,
  31: /// because that is what gravity is in.
  32: pub const CM_TO_M: f32 = 0.01;
  33: 
  34: /// How finely a panel outline's curves are sampled before meshing. The mesher
  35: /// resamples anyway, so this only has to be fine enough not to lose the shape
  36: /// of a curved edge -- a neckline, an armhole.
  37: const CURVE_SAMPLES_PER_CM: f64 = 0.5;
  38: 
  39: /// Simulation settings the tab exposes.
  40: #[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq)]
  41: pub struct FitSettings {
  42:     /// Target mesh edge, in centimetres. The resolution knob: it decides the
  43:     /// particle count and the finest fold the fabric can make.
  44:     pub resolution_cm: f32,
  45:     pub substeps: u32,
  46:     /// How far a garment particle is held off the body surface.
  47:     pub body_offset_cm: f32,
  48:     pub self_collision: bool,
  49:     pub gravity: bool,
  50:     /// The height, in centimetres, of the body the pattern was drawn for.
  51:     ///
  52:     /// A body model and a sewing pattern agree on nothing -- not the unit, not
  53:     /// where the origin is -- so the one thing they can be matched on is how
  54:     /// tall the person is. The pattern's own measurements say; the model is
  55:     /// scaled to it.
  56:     pub body_height_cm: f32,
  57:     /// Substeps between the host-side swept-contact passes `fabelgeist-shell` runs
  58:     /// for self-collision, or 0 to leave contact to the GPU kernels.
  59:     ///
  60:     /// Each pass reads the garment back and waits for the GPU, so this is what
  61:     /// an interleaved step costs. Measured at 12 substeps: every substep
  62:     /// (prism's default) drapes the MHR test body in 542 ms a frame, once a
  63:     /// frame in 57 ms, off in 9.3 ms, and all three drape it the same. A
  64:     /// garment crumpling onto the floor is where they part: every substep
  65:     /// keeps its edges within 50% of rest, off leaves one at 50%, and once a
  66:     /// frame stretches one by 235% -- a sparse pass is worse than none.
  67:     pub host_contact_interval: u32,
  68: }
  69: 
  70: impl Default for FitSettings {

1: //! Follicles: where hair grows, which way it grows, and what it grows as.
2: //!
3: //! Hair does not leave the scalp straight out. Each follicle is slanted, and
4: //! over the scalp the slants line up into a *growth pattern*: in most people
5: //! a whorl at the crown -- a spiral, usually clockwise seen from above --
6: //! from which hair runs forward over the top, down the sides and down the
7: //! back. Some have two whorls, a cowlick at the front hairline, or hair
8: //! that grows forward or back all over. Short hair shows the pattern as it
9: //! is; longer hair is combed into a style, but near the root it keeps its
10: //! follicle's direction for a centimetre or so (a cowlick stands up where
11: //! the comb goes against it).
12: //!
13: //! [`Follicles`] holds the pattern ([`Growth`], placed and shaped by the
14: //! whorl's position, spiral and handedness) and what else the follicles
15: //! decide: the angle hair leaves the scalp at and how much it varies, how
16: //! far the follicle's direction holds against the comb, how coily hair
17: //! wanders, how thick it is, how evenly it covers the scalp, the hairline's
18: //! shape and softness, and pattern loss. [`GrowthField`] is the pattern
19: //! placed on a head: a direction at every point of the scalp, for the guides
20: //! ([`crate::hairdo`]) and for every strand ([`crate::ops::Orient`]).

34:     /// forward over the top, down the sides and the back.
35:     Whorl,

37:     /// between them.

40:     /// lifts the hair there.
41:     Cowlick,

1: //! Grooming on the GPU.
2: //!
3: //! The groom's stack is embarrassingly parallel -- every operation after
4: //! interpolation works on each strand alone, and a head is a hundred
5: //! thousand strands of up to two hundred and fifty-six points -- so it runs
6: //! as compute kernels, and what it grows stays on the GPU: the renderer
7: //! draws the levels of detail straight from the buffers the kernels wrote.
8: //!
9: //! [`GpuGroomer`] holds the kernels, on the compute layer: one
10: //! [`KernelBatch`] a groom (every dispatch into one encoder, one submit),
11: //! [`PrefixSum`] to compact the roots and the cards, its
12: //! [`RadixSort`] for the shuffled strand order the levels of detail share,
13: //! and its spatial hash grid for the roots about each vertex of the head.
14: //! The kernels themselves ([`wgsl`]) mirror the host operations in
15: //! [`crate::ops`] line for line; the host operations remain, the reference
16: //! the kernels are checked against and the path for a machine without a
17: //! GPU.
18: //!
19: //! * [`GpuGroomer::grow_look`] grows a [`crate::Look`] whole, and
20: //!   [`GpuGroomer::grow`] any [`Groom`] from [`Guides`]: a hairdo's, grown
21: //!   there, or the host's. A hairdo's guide roots are placed as the host
22: //!   places them -- candidates hashed by index, kept greedily in order by
23: //!   one workgroup -- and each guide is combed by a workgroup of its own,
24: //!   its lanes sampling the head's field together and drawing the same
25: //!   numbers as the host ([`crate::rng::Stream`]), so the guides come out
26: //!   as the host's to a micrometre or so. The operations before
27: //!   interpolation (the drape, a solve per strand, with a strand's joints
28: //!   in workgroup memory; the shrinkwrap) run on the guides, the rest on
29: //!   the strands.
30: //! * [`GpuGroomer::cut_scalp`] cuts the scalp they grow on ([`GpuScalp`]):
31: //!   surface nets over the head's field and the part above the hairline,
32: //!   to the host's own triangles, in the host's order -- a count, a scan
33: //!   and an emit for the triangles, vertices numbered by where they are
34: //!   first used, the running area added up in the host's order, the open
35: //!   edges found by sorting. [`GpuGroomer::upload_scalp`] takes any other
36: //!   (DiffLocks' `scalp.ply`, say). Roots are placed by area over the scalp
37: //!   in one pass -- each triangle its share, spread by a low-discrepancy
38: //!   sequence -- thinned by the density masks and compacted by a scan.
39: //!   Clump guides are chosen on a grid, the lowest-hashed strand of each
40: //!   cell leading it. A strand sampling its guide walks the guide from the
41: //!   root, transporting its frame as it goes, so no frames are stored.
42: //! * [`GpuGroomer::lods`] prepares a grown groom for drawing: sorted into
43: //!   the shuffled order, occlusion baked into a volume and every point,
44: //!   each strand level resampled (and kept off the head), the cards cut
45: //!   from the locks, and how much hair covers each vertex of the head.
46: //! * [`GpuGroomer::simulate`] makes real-time physics for it ([`GpuSim`]):
47: //!   [`crate::sim::HairSim`]'s rods, bound and stepped where they are
48: //!   drawn, a substep a dispatch (an invocation a strand solving its own
49: //!   implicit steps), and meeting each other -- the volume and
50: //!   friction on a density grid in the head's frame, collisions found by
51: //!   samples sorted into a grid of cells and resolved segment against
52: //!   segment. [`GpuGroomer::resimulate`] moves it to another level of
53: //!   detail, its motion carried across.
54: //! * [`GpuGroomer::upload`] brings strands made elsewhere -- a DiffLocks
55: //!   sample, a host groom -- to the GPU, to prepare and draw the same way.
56: //!
57: //! A sweep along a strand keeps its points in registers or in the kernel's
58: //! own output, never in a large local array: dynamically indexed
59: //! `array<vec3<f32>, 32>`s came out differently from run to run on the same
60: //! input, and the tests grow every groom twice to hold that down.
61: //!
62: //! ```no_run
63: //! # fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
64: //! use fabelgeist_hair::gpu::{GpuGroomer, headless_context};

1: //! A hairdo: follicles, a cut and a style, and the guides they grow.
2: //!
3: //! DiffLocks' artists drew 75 base hairstyles by hand in Blender, each about
4: //! fifty guide strands giving only "the overall shape and direction of the
5: //! hair"; the randomisation adds everything else. Those guides are not
6: //! published. Here a base style is three independent choices -- the
7: //! [`Follicles`] (which way hair grows), the [`Haircut`] (how long it is)
8: //! and the [`Hairstyle`] (how it is combed) -- and every guide is grown as a
9: //! strand of hair would lie:
10: //!
11: //! * **Out of the scalp.** A strand leaves its follicle the way it is
12: //!   combed, at the follicle's angle to the scalp (lifted as the style lifts
13: //!   it), and rises over a few centimetres to its layer: the hair under it.
14: //!   (Which way the follicle itself points shows in the first centimetre of
15: //!   every strand, [`crate::ops::Orient`], and in how hair lies where the
16: //!   style leaves it as it grows.) Hair rooted higher up -- nearer the part
17: //!   or the crown -- lies over hair rooted lower down, so the layer's height
18: //!   grows from nothing at the hairline to the style's volume at the top.
19: //! * **On the head.** Lying on its layer, a strand follows the style's comb
20: //!   (away from a part, back, forward, to a tie, or as it grows), turned
21: //!   into the layer's tangent plane, and slides downhill as much as the
22: //!   hair still to come weighs on it: long hair on the side of the head
23: //!   runs down it, short hair keeps the way it was combed. In front of the
24: //!   face, hair keeps to its comb until it is past the face.
25: //! * **Off the head.** Free -- past the head's widest, or lifted off it -- a
26: //!   strand is a cantilever: gravity bends it with the curvature a rod's own
27: //!   weight gives, `(L - s)^2 / (2 L_g^3)` for `L - s` of it still to come
28: //!   and `L_g` the style's hold (about 5 cm for a strand, more for a styled
29: //!   or curly lock). Long hair drops straight down where it leaves the
30: //!   head; short hair stands out.
31: //! * **Cut.** A strand is as long as the cut makes hair at its root, and
32: //!   ends where it crosses the cut's line (the hemline, or a fringe's line
33: //!   at the brows) or the cut's dome.
34: //! * **Ties.** A ponytail's, bun's or braid's strands run over the scalp to
35: //!   the tie, then become the tail, the coil or one of the braid's three

1: //! Strand hair after Rosu et al., *DiffLocks: Generating 3D Hair from a
2: //! Single Image using Diffusion Models* (CVPR 2025) -- the synthetic-data
3: //! half of it: how its 40K hairstyles are made, and then how to draw them,
4: //! from film to phone.
5: //!
6: //! # Making hair
7: //!
8: //! DiffLocks grows every hairstyle in Blender with geometry nodes. A base
9: //! style is a few dozen hand-drawn guide strands; a stack of Blender's hair
10: //! node groups interpolates them to ~100K strands over the scalp, then
11: //! clumps, curls and noises them -- each several times at different scales
12: //! -- shrinkwraps them off the body and drapes them under random gravity and
13: //! wind. 110 parameters, each drawn from a range, make every sample
14: //! different. The same pipeline here:
15: //!
16: //! * [`Strands`]: curves of equal point count with the attributes the node
17: //!   groups pass between them (root UV and normal, a stable ID, the parting
18: //!   group, the guide map).
19: //! * [`ops`]: the node groups themselves, written out from their node
20: //!   graphs -- `Interpolate Hair Curves`, `Clump Hair Curves`, `Curl Hair
21: //!   Curves`, `Frizz Hair Curves`, `Hair Curves Noise`, `Trim`, `Smooth`,
22: //!   `Shrinkwrap Hair Curves` with `Restore Curve Segment Length`, `Create
23: //!   Guide Index Map`, `Set Hair Curve Profile` and their `shape_range`
24: //!   falloff -- plus waves ([`ops::Wave`]), each strand's root turned to its
25: //!   follicle ([`ops::Orient`]) and the drape ([`ops::Settle`]), run in
26: //!   parallel over strands.
27: //! * [`Groom`]: a stack of operations, serialisable, the recipe of one
28: //!   hairstyle; [`Look`] a stack built from the few knobs that mean
29: //!   something to a person, in DiffLocks' order, and drawn at random the way
30: //!   the dataset draws.
31: //! * [`Hairdo`]: what shapes the guides, as three choices made apart --
32: //!   the [`Follicles`] (the growth pattern, [`Growth`]: a crown whorl, two,
33: //!   a cowlick, forward, back...; the angle hair leaves the scalp at, how
34: //!   far it keeps its follicle's direction, how thick it is, how evenly it
35: //!   covers the scalp, the [`Hairline`]'s shape), the [`Haircut`] (lengths
36: //!   over the head, a hemline, clippers, a fringe, a dome: [`Cut`] names
37: //!   the usual ones) and the [`Hairstyle`] (parted, swept, slicked back,
38: //!   stood up, tied: [`Arrangement`]) -- grown as guides on a [`Head`] (a
39: //!   mannequin bust as a distance field, which is also the scalp,
40: //!   [`Surface`], and the collider, [`Collider`]). [`Preset`] names
41: //!   twenty-four hairdos: every kind of hair the paper's figures show
42: //!   ([`Preset::PAPER`]: bob, crop, long, shag, bowl cut, ringlets, afro,
43: //!   quiff, balding and more) and some it lacks (ponytail, bun, braid,
44: //!   dreadlocks, mohawk).
45: //! * [`HairMaterial`]: the Chiang hair BSDF's parameters, melanin and
46: //!   redness as Blender's Principled Hair takes them.
47: //! * [`dataset`] and the `hair-dataset` binary: samples on disk in the
48: //!   dataset's own layout (`full_strands.npz`, the density map, metadata,
49: //!   a render), and [`export`]: NumPy, USC-HairSalon `.data`, PLY scalps.
50: //!
51: //! # Drawing hair
52: //!
53: //! [`HairLods`] prepares a groom once into every form it can be drawn in --
54: //! the strands at several point counts in one shuffled order (so any prefix
55: //! is an even sample, and fewer strands is just a smaller count), hair cards
56: //! cut from the groom's own locks with a painted atlas, and occlusion baked
57: //! into every point. A [`LodPolicy`] picks the form from the head's size on
58: //! screen for a target -- cinematic, desktop or mobile -- with its shading.
59: //! [`render::HairRenderer`] draws it: camera-facing ribbons from a storage
60: //! buffer, Marschner's lobes in Karis' fit (or Kajiya-Kay on mobile), deep
61: //! opacity maps from the key light, stochastic transparency so sub-pixel
62: //! strands add up to their true density, and a jittered running mean that
63: //! converges to a supersampled still. `hair-viewer` shows it all live.
64: //!
65: //! # Moving hair
66: //!
67: //! [`sim::HairSim`] runs real-time physics, optionally: some of the groom's
68: //! strands simulated as elastic rods ([`rod`]: Cosserat rods with hair's
69: //! own stiffness and mass, under gravity, in the air, clamped in follicles
70: //! a moving head carries, kept off its distance field, each step implicit
71: //! and solved exactly; the groom their equilibrium under gravity), every
72: //! drawn strand following the ones nearest its root in a compute pass, and
73: //! moving frames blended over time so the stochastic coverage does not
74: //! sparkle. On the GPU
75: //! ([`gpu::GpuSim`]) the strands also meet: hair denser than at rest is
76: //! pushed apart (its volume kept), hair moving through hair drags it along,
77: //! and strands collide, segment against segment. How many strands, of how
78: //! many points, is a level of detail of its own ([`sim::SimLevel`]), chosen
79: //! by the head's size on screen like the drawing's.
80: //!
81: //! # On the GPU
82: //!
83: //! All of it runs on the GPU as well ([`gpu`], the `gpu` feature): the
84: //! guides, the groom, its levels of detail and cards, the head's cover and
85: //! the physics are compute kernels on the compute layer, and what they
86: //! make is drawn from the buffers they wrote -- a hundred thousand strands
87: //! grown and prepared in tens of milliseconds, where the host takes a
88: //! second or two; the scalp they root on is cut there too, when the
89: //! hairline changes. The viewer, the dataset and the snapshots groom
90: //! there. The host path stays, the reference the kernels are tested
91: //! against (the scalp to its triangles, the guides to a micrometre) and the
92: //! way without a GPU.
93: //!
94: //! # Where this departs from the paper
95: //!
96: //! * **The body.** DiffLocks grows hair on the SMPL-X scalp and collides it
97: //!   with the SMPL-X body; SMPL-X is not ours to ship. The [`Head`] is a
98: //!   bust of unioned ellipsoids and capsules; any scalp with a UV map loads
99: //!   in its place ([`Surface::from_ply`] reads DiffLocks' `scalp.ply`).
100: //! * **The base styles** are 75 hand-drawn sets of guides in the paper and
101: //!   not published. Here each style is grown: every guide leaves its
102: //!   follicle as the growth pattern points, rises to the layer of hair
103: //!   beneath it, lies along the head as combed while it is supported, and
104: //!   bends as a cantilever under its own weight once free, until the cut
105: //!   ends it ([`hairdo`]). Every strand's root is then turned to its own
106: //!   follicle ([`ops::Orient`]), which interpolating guides a few
107: //!   centimetres apart would blur.
108: //! * **Interpolation** takes a strand count rather than a density, fades
109: //!   `Follow Surface Normal`'s turn out along the strand (Blender turns the
110: //!   whole strand, which on a curved scalp swings long hair's tips out), and
111: //!   blends only guides whose courses agree: the mean of a guide combed
112: //!   left and one combed right would run down the face between them.
113: //! * **The drape** is each strand's static equilibrium as an elastic rod
114: //!   against the head's field ([`ops::Settle`]), not Blender's cloth solver,
115: //!   and applies the *change* from standard gravity and still air -- so it
116: //!   blows and lifts a style without sagging it into another. It runs on
117: //!   the guides, and the full groom inherits it.
118: //! * **Frizz and noise** are Blender's, with two changes: frizz takes a
119: //!   share of flyaway strands (the rest barely wander) and can wander
120: //!   smoothly, and the look uses noise as offsets, not Blender's cumulative
121: //!   walk, whose reach grows with the point count.
122: //! * **Rendering.** DiffLocks path-traces the Chiang BSDF under HDRIs.
123: //!   Here rendering is rasterised and real time; the Chiang absorption is
124: //!   exported with every sample for an offline renderer, and the real-time
125: //!   colour is Chiang's colour mapping over a quarter of it, matched to
126: //!   Cycles by eye ([`HairMaterial::base_color`]).
127: //!
128: //! ```no_run
129: //! use fabelgeist_hair::{Arrangement, Cut, Growth, HairLods, Haircut, Head, LodSettings, Look, Preset};

1: //! `Interpolate Hair Curves V2`: from a few guides to a full head of hair.
2: //!
3: //! The node group scatters points over the scalp -- Poisson-disk, as dense
4: //! as `Density` asks, thinned by a density mask (DiffLocks' balding patterns)
5: //! -- and grows a strand from each by `Interpolate Curves`: the shapes of the
6: //! nearest guides (`Interpolation Guides` of them, only those in the same
7: //! parting group), each taken relative to its own root and blended by
8: //! distance, placed at the new root. With `Follow Surface Normal` each
9: //! guide's shape is first turned from its root's normal to the new root's,
10: //! so a shape combed on the crown still lies along the head at the temple.
11: //! Strands closer than `Distance to Guides` to a guide's root are dropped.
12: //!
13: //! Where it departs: the node group takes a density per unit area; here the
14: //! stack asks for a strand count (the dataset's "~100K strands") and the
15: //! Poisson radius follows from it and the scalp's area. And it blends only
16: //! guides that agree ([`Interpolate::divergence`]): the mean of a guide
17: //! combed left and one combed right is a strand combed straight down
18: //! between them -- across the face, from the front hairline -- where real
19: //! hair would part and go one way or the other.
20: 
21: use crate::identity::PartingGroup;
22: use crate::identity::StrandId;
23: use fabelgeist_math::Vec3;
24: use rayon::prelude::*;
25: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

27: use crate::grid::PointGrid;

30: use crate::strands::{Attachment, Strands, rotate, safe_normalize};

32: #[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]
33: pub struct Interpolate {
34:     /// How many strands to grow (before the density mask thins them).
35:     pub count: usize,
36:     /// Blend the nearest this many guides (`Interpolation Guides`).
37:     pub neighbors: usize,
38:     /// Drop new strands closer than this to a guide's root (0 keeps all).
39:     pub distance_to_guides: f32,
40:     /// Space roots out (`Poisson Disk Distribution`) rather than scatter
41:     /// them independently.
42:     pub poisson: bool,
43:     /// Turn each guide's shape from its root normal to the new root's.
44:     pub follow_surface_normal: bool,
45:     /// Along how much of the strand the turn fades out, metres. Blender
46:     /// turns the whole strand; on a curved scalp that swings long hair's
47:     /// tips out by the angle between neighbouring roots.
48:     pub follow_length: f32,
49:     /// Keep interpolation within parting groups (`Part by Texture`).
50:     pub parting: Parting,
51:     /// Blend only guides whose shapes agree with the nearest one's: a
52:     /// guide is left out where its course strays from the nearest guide's
53:     /// by more than this share of how far that one has come (0: blend all).
54:     /// Where combing diverges, strands follow one side or the other, and
55:     /// the hair parts there as hair does.
56:     #[serde(default)]
57:     pub divergence: f32,
58:     /// How likely a root is to be kept, over the scalp.
59:     pub density: DensityMask,
60:     /// How unevenly roots cover the scalp, 0 to 1: patches a few
61:     /// centimetres across thinned by up to this much.
62:     #[serde(default)]
63:     pub patchiness: f32,
64:     /// Over how far in from the scalp's edge -- the hairline -- roots thin
65:     /// out and strands grow finer, metres (0: a sharp edge).
66:     #[serde(default)]
67:     pub edge: f32,
68:     /// Keep the guides themselves among the strands.
69:     pub keep_guides: bool,
70:     /// Root radius of the new strands, metres.
71:     pub radius: f32,
72:     pub seed: i32,
73: }
74: 
75: impl Default for Interpolate {
76:     fn default() -> Self {
77:         Self {
78:             count: 30_000,
79:             neighbors: 4,
80:             distance_to_guides: 0.0,
81:             poisson: true,
82:             follow_surface_normal: true,
83:             follow_length: 0.05,
84:             parting: Parting::None,
85:             divergence: 0.0,
86:             density: DensityMask::Uniform,
87:             patchiness: 0.0,
88:             edge: 0.0,
89:             keep_guides: false,
90:             radius: 35e-6,
91:             seed: 0,
92:         }
93:     }
94: }

96: /// Where hair parts: a plane through the head (the part line is where it

98: /// kept apart; behind `until` (a `z`, towards the back) the part has ended
99: /// and roots take from both sides.
100: #[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
101: pub enum Parting {
102:     #[default]
103:     None,
104:     Plane {
105:         normal: [f32; 3],
106:         offset: f32,
107:         until: f32,
108:     },
109:     /// Sectors round the head, the front one in the middle: a braid's

86:     preview: &mut SoapRestPreview,
87:     sources: RestSupplySources<'_>,
88: ) {

91:         personal,
92:         shared,
93:         personal_amounts,
94:         party_amounts,
95:         definitions,
96:         personalities,
97:         party_id,
98:     } = sources;
99:     let living_ids = members
100:         .iter()
101:         .filter(|member| member.alive)

103:         .collect::<std::collections::BTreeSet<_>>();
104:     let is_temperate = |character_id| {
105:         personalities
106:             .iter()
107:             .find(|(id, _)| *id == character_id)
108:             .is_some_and(|(_, personality)| {
109:                 personality.temperance == crate::spacetimedb::Temperance::Temperate
110:             })
111:     };
112:     let alcoholic_ids = definitions
113:         .iter()
114:         .filter(|item| {
115:             item.alcohol_potable
116:                 && item.alcohol_serving_ml > 0
117:                 && item.alcohol_abv_basis_points > 0
118:                 && !item.alcohol_disinfectant_focused
119:         })
120:         .map(|item| item.id.as_str())
121:         .collect::<std::collections::BTreeSet<_>>();
122: 
123:     let personal_soap = personal
124:         .iter()
125:         .filter(|stack| living_ids.contains(&stack.character_id) && stack.item_id == SOFT_SOAP_ID)
126:         .map(|stack| {
127:             personal_amounts
128:                 .iter()
129:                 .find(|state| state.inventory_item_id == stack.id)
130:                 .map_or(0, |state| soap_uses(state.remaining_fraction_micros))
131:         })
132:         .sum::<u32>();

134:         shared
135:             .iter()
136:             .filter(|stack| stack.party_id == party_id && stack.item_id == SOFT_SOAP_ID)
137:             .map(|stack| {
138:                 party_amounts
139:                     .iter()
140:                     .find(|state| state.party_inventory_item_id == stack.id)
141:                     .map_or(0, |state| soap_uses(state.remaining_fraction_micros))
142:             })
143:             .sum::<u32>()
144:     });
145:     preview.available_units = personal_soap.saturating_add(shared_soap);
146: 
147:     let personal_alcohol = personal.iter().any(|stack| {
148:         living_ids.contains(&stack.character_id)
149:             && personal_amounts.iter().any(|state| {
150:                 state.inventory_item_id == stack.id
151:                     && !consumable_fraction(state.remaining_fraction_micros).is_zero()
152:             })
153:             && alcoholic_ids.contains(stack.item_id.as_str())
154:     });
155:     let personal_drink = personal.iter().any(|stack| {
156:         living_ids.contains(&stack.character_id)
157:             && !is_temperate(stack.character_id)
158:             && personal_amounts.iter().any(|state| {
159:                 state.inventory_item_id == stack.id
160:                     && !consumable_fraction(state.remaining_fraction_micros).is_zero()
161:             })
162:             && alcoholic_ids.contains(stack.item_id.as_str())
163:     });
164:     let shared_alcohol = party_id.is_some_and(|party_id| {
165:         shared.iter().any(|stack| {
166:             stack.party_id == party_id
167:                 && party_amounts.iter().any(|state| {
168:                     state.party_inventory_item_id == stack.id
169:                         && !consumable_fraction(state.remaining_fraction_micros).is_zero()
170:                 })
171:                 && alcoholic_ids.contains(stack.item_id.as_str())
172:         })
173:     });
174:     let has_non_temperate_member = living_ids
175:         .iter()
176:         .any(|character_id| !is_temperate(*character_id));
177:     preview.alcohol_available = personal_alcohol || shared_alcohol;
178:     preview.alcohol_will_be_consumed =
179:         personal_drink || (shared_alcohol && has_non_temperate_member);

182: pub(super) fn calculate_soap_rest_preview(
183:     members: &[CharacterView],
184:     filth: &[CharacterFilth],
185:     personal: &[InventoryItem],
186:     shared: &[PartyInventoryItem],
187:     personal_amounts: &[InventoryItemAmount],
188:     party_amounts: &[PartyItemAmount],
189:     party_id: Option<&str>,
190: ) -> SoapRestPreview {
191:     let mut personal_units = 0_u32;
192:     let mut need_after_personal = 0_u32;
193:     for member in members.iter().filter(|member| member.alive) {
194:         let amount = filth
195:             .iter()
196:             .filter(|deposit| deposit.character_id == member.id)
197:             .map(|deposit| u32::from(deposit.amount))
198:             .sum::<u32>();
199:         let needed = amount;
200:         let available = personal
201:             .iter()
202:             .filter(|stack| stack.character_id == member.id && stack.item_id == SOFT_SOAP_ID)
203:             .map(|stack| {
204:                 personal_amounts
205:                     .iter()
206:                     .find(|state| state.inventory_item_id == stack.id)
207:                     .map_or(0, |state| soap_uses(state.remaining_fraction_micros))
208:             })
209:             .sum::<u32>();
210:         let used = needed.min(available);
211:         personal_units = personal_units.saturating_add(used);
212:         need_after_personal = need_after_personal.saturating_add(needed.saturating_sub(used));
213:     }
214:     let shared_available = party_id.map_or(0, |party_id| {
215:         shared
216:             .iter()
217:             .filter(|stack| stack.party_id == party_id && stack.item_id == SOFT_SOAP_ID)
218:             .map(|stack| {
219:                 party_amounts
220:                     .iter()
221:                     .find(|state| state.party_inventory_item_id == stack.id)
222:                     .map_or(0, |state| soap_uses(state.remaining_fraction_micros))
223:             })
224:             .sum()
225:     });
226:     let shared_units = need_after_personal.min(shared_available);
227:     SoapRestPreview {
228:         total_units: personal_units.saturating_add(shared_units),
229:         personal_units,
230:         shared_units,
231:         ..SoapRestPreview::default()
232:     }
233: }

457: pub(super) fn quality_score(
458:     frames: &[FrameSample],
459:     scenarios: &[ScenarioMetrics],
460:     validation: &AnimationCaptureValidation,
461: ) -> AnimationValueResult<QualityScore> {
462:     let catastrophic_foot_displacement_failed = catastrophic_foot_displacement(frames);
463:     let anatomical_invalid_joints_failed = scenarios.iter().any(|metrics| {
464:         procedural_leg_solver_gates_apply(&metrics.scenario)
465:             && !(metrics.pose.minimum_knee_flexion_degrees.measured().is_some_and(|angle| angle.degrees() >= 3.9)
466:                 && metrics.pose.minimum_knee_hemisphere_dot.measured().is_some_and(|dot| dot.value() >= 0.0)
467:                 && metrics.pose.minimum_signed_foot_track_metres.measured().is_some_and(|value| value.metres() >= -0.01)
468:                 && metrics.pose.minimum_inter_foot_separation_metres.measured().is_some_and(|value| *value >= metrics.expected.inter_foot_separation)
469:                 && metrics.pose.maximum_knee_foot_yaw_offset_degrees.measured().is_some_and(|angle| angle.degrees() <= 22.6))
470:     });
471:     let contact_foot_airborne_failed = !validation.no_ground_penetration
472:         || !validation.run_flight_valid
473:         || !validation.reported_support_contacts_valid
474:         || !validation.run_contact_acquisition_valid;
475:     let both_feet_behind_hips_failed = both_feet_behind_hips(frames);
476:     let guard_step_liveness_failed = !validation.raised_guard_step_liveness_valid;
477:     let foot_dragging_failed = scenarios.iter().any(|metrics| {
478:         !metrics.continuity.measured().is_some_and(|continuity| {
479:             continuity.maximum_supported_foot_slip_metres_per_frame.when_applicable(|slip| *slip <= metrics.expected.supported_slip)
480:         }) || !metrics.maximum_planted_foot_drift_metres.when_applicable(|drift| *drift <= metrics.expected.planted_drift)
481:     });
482:     let jitter_and_jerk_failed = !validation.jitter_validation.diagnostics_complete
483:         || validation
484:             .jitter_validation
485:             .unacceptable_final_incident_count
486:             > 0;
487:     let categories = QualityCategories {
488:         catastrophic_foot_displacement_failed,
489:         guard_step_liveness_failed,
490:         anatomical_invalid_joints_failed,
491:         contact_foot_airborne_failed,
492:         both_feet_behind_hips_failed,
493:         foot_dragging_failed,
494:         jitter_and_jerk_failed,
495:     };
496:     let weighted_defect_score = weighted_defect_score(&categories);
497:     let capture_complete = validation.all_scenarios_complete && validation.all_artifacts_written;
498:     let quality_percent = if capture_complete {
499:         Observation::Measured(QualityPercent::from_fraction(UnitInterval::from_fraction(
500:             1.0 - f32::from(weighted_defect_score) / 31.0,
501:         )?))
502:     } else {
503:         Observation::Unavailable(UnavailableReason::IncompleteCapture)
504:     };
505:     Ok(QualityScore {
506:         weighted_defect_score,
507:         maximum_weighted_defect_score: 31,
508:         quality_percent,
509:         acceptance_passed: validation_passed(validation),
510:         categories,
511:     })
512: }
513: 
514: pub(super) fn weighted_defect_score(categories: &QualityCategories) -> u8 {
515:     if categories.catastrophic_foot_displacement_failed || categories.guard_step_liveness_failed {
516:         31
517:     } else {
518:         u8::from(categories.anatomical_invalid_joints_failed) * 16
519:             + u8::from(categories.contact_foot_airborne_failed) * 8
520:             + u8::from(categories.both_feet_behind_hips_failed) * 4
521:             + u8::from(categories.foot_dragging_failed) * 2
522:             + u8::from(categories.jitter_and_jerk_failed)
523:     }
524: }

42: /// Specifies the range of distances that this entity must be from the camera in
43: /// order to be rendered.
44: ///
45: /// This is also known as *hierarchical level of detail* or *HLOD*.
46: ///
47: /// Use this component when you want to render a high-polygon mesh when the
48: /// camera is close and a lower-polygon mesh when the camera is far away. This
49: /// is a common technique for improving performance, because fine details are
50: /// hard to see in a mesh at a distance. To avoid an artifact known as *popping*
51: /// between levels, each level has a *margin*, within which the object
52: /// transitions gradually from invisible to visible using a dithering effect.
53: ///
54: /// You can also use this feature to replace multiple meshes with a single mesh
55: /// when the camera is distant. This is the reason for the term "*hierarchical*
56: /// level of detail". Reducing the number of meshes can be useful for reducing
57: /// drawcall count. Note that you must place the [`VisibilityRange`] component
58: /// on each entity you want to be part of a LOD group, as [`VisibilityRange`]
59: /// isn't automatically propagated down to children.
60: ///
61: /// A typical use of this feature might look like this:
62: ///
63: /// | Entity                  | `start_margin` | `end_margin` |
64: /// |-------------------------|----------------|--------------|
65: /// | Root                    | N/A            | N/A          |
66: /// | ├─ High-poly mesh       | [0, 0)         | [20, 25)     |
67: /// | ├─ Low-poly mesh        | [20, 25)       | [70, 75)     |
68: /// | └─ Billboard *imposter* | [70, 75)       | [150, 160)   |
69: ///
70: /// With this setup, the user will see a high-poly mesh when the camera is
71: /// closer than 20 units. As the camera zooms out, between 20 units to 25 units,
72: /// the high-poly mesh will gradually fade to a low-poly mesh. When the camera
73: /// is 70 to 75 units away, the low-poly mesh will fade to a single textured
74: /// quad. And between 150 and 160 units, the object fades away entirely. Note
75: /// that the `end_margin` of a higher LOD is always identical to the
76: /// `start_margin` of the next lower LOD; this is important for the crossfade
77: /// effect to function properly.
78: #[derive(Component, Clone, PartialEq, Default, Reflect)]
79: #[reflect(Component, PartialEq, Hash, Clone)]
80: pub struct VisibilityRange {
81:     /// The range of distances, in world units, between which this entity will
82:     /// smoothly fade into view as the camera zooms out.
83:     ///

199: impl VisibleEntityRanges {
200:     /// Clears out the [`VisibleEntityRanges`] in preparation for a new frame.

202:         self.views.clear();
203:         self.entities.clear();

216:             return false;
217:         };
218:         let Some(view_index) = self.views.get(&view) else {
219:             return false;
220:         };

222:     }

250:         visible_entity_ranges.views.insert(view, view_index);

254:     // Check each entity/view pair. Only consider entities with

275:             // Invisible entities have no entry at all in the hash map. This speeds
276:             // up checks slightly in this common case.
277:             if visibility != 0 {
278:                 par_local.borrow_local_mut().push((entity, visibility));
279:             }
280:         },
